title: Adic reconstruction
statement:
Fix the global finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Here integral coefficients mean modules over the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, and the reductions are $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}(A_{E,n})_Y\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Use integral pullback and completed tensor [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], the coefficient twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and the integral exceptional inverse image defined by derived inverse limits of the compatible finite-level functors [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

The comparisons $\gamma_{f,K_n}$ of [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] commute with the normalization isomorphisms and give a morphism of the finite-coefficient normalized systems. After restriction to $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ this family admits a morphism in the derived category of strict towers [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], and induces an isomorphism
$$Lf^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!K$$
in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$ whose reduction in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ is exactly $\gamma_{f,K_n}$ under the canonical reduction identifications for every $n$. No uniqueness of a coherent lift of the levelwise family is asserted.

proof.text: Write $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ and $B_{n,W}=(A_{E,n})_W$. Write $f_n$ for $f$ acting with the finite coefficient sheaves $B_{n,Y},B_{n,X}$. Put $U=Lf^*K(d)[2d]$ and $U_n=Lf_n^*K_n(d)[2d]$. Integral pullback and completed tensor preserve bounded constructibility and have the stated canonical reductions by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible]. By [prop-weil-twist-preserves] the integral twist is a locally free rank-one invertible $R_X$-module; hence locally it is the coefficient sheaf and tensoring by it preserves the same cohomological and Tor intervals. The integral twist's reductions are the finite twists by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]; for its positive power $d$, trivializing the rank-one sheaf reduces both this assertion and the tensor comparison to $R_X\otimes_{R_X}B_{n,X}=B_{n,X}$. If $[a,b]$ is the common Tor interval of the $K_n$ from [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] gives that interval for every $Lf_n^*K_n$. Tensoring by the locally free twist leaves it unchanged, and shifting by $[2d]$ changes it to $[a-2d,b-2d]$, since $\mathcal H^i(C[2d])=\mathcal H^{i+2d}(C)$. Finite pullback is the exact module inverse image in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], so it preserves the input cohomological window. The rank-one twist also preserves it; the shift changes its endpoints by minus $2d$. Thus $U\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and its canonical reduction is $U_n$ at every level. This proves the finiteness actually needed; it does not infer common integral local models from boundedness alone.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal U_\bullet$ be the derived reduction tower of $U$. Its normalization maps are those of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Put $V_n=Rf_n^!K_n$ and let $\mathcal V_\bullet$ be the coherent tower used to define $V=Rf^!K=R\lim\mathcal V_\bullet$ in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. For $m\geq n$, its normalization is the finite-reduction comparison $\operatorname{red}_{m,n,X}(Rf_m^!K_m)\simeq Rf_n^!(\operatorname{red}_{m,n,Y}K_m)$ of [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity], followed by $Rf_n^!$ of the normalization $\operatorname{red}_{m,n,Y}K_m\simeq K_n$. The compatible finite-level functors in the exceptional-inverse-image definition supply the coherent transitions; the original quotient cocycle identifies successive reductions with direct reduction. In the notation of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], both $\mathcal U_\bullet$ and $\mathcal V_\bullet$ are normalized DVR towers over $R_X$. No common local model or preservation of a common stratification by $Rf^!$ is assumed.

proof.text: Set $g_n=\gamma_{f,K_n}:U_n\to V_n$. The commuting square of [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity] says $\rho^V_{m,n}\circ\operatorname{red}_{m,n,X}(g_m)=g_n\circ\rho^U_{m,n}$. Applying the normalization of $K$ uses naturality of the purity map in its coefficient object: in the composite defining it in [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], twist reassociation is natural, the isomorphism from the fixed dualizing object to the twist is independent of $K$, and the final canonical tensor-formula map is natural. Precompose the displayed equation with the scalar-extension unit and restrict coefficients to $R_X$; this gives $t^V_n\circ\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}(g_{n+1})=\operatorname{Res}_n(g_n)\circ t^U_n$. Thus it is a morphism of the evaluated inverse sequences. By [lem-weil-pbc-sequential-tower-evaluation-full] choose a lift $G:\mathcal U_\bullet\to\mathcal V_\bullet$ whose evaluations are these maps. Every $g_n$ is an isomorphism by [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity]. The lifting theorem asserts existence, not uniqueness of $G$.

proof.text: Apply the total derived inverse-limit functor of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] to $G$, and write $F=R\lim G:R\lim\mathcal U_\bullet\to V$. Its natural Roos triangles give a morphism of triangles with second and third components $\prod_n\operatorname{Res}_n(g_n)$. The hypothesis of [lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso] therefore holds, so $F$ is an isomorphism. Since $U$ is derived complete, [def-weil-derived-complete] supplies a Roos triangle starting with the scalar-extension units $c^U_n$. Rotate this triangle and the Roos triangle of $R\lim\mathcal U_\bullet$, apply the triangulated axiom TR3 to the identity maps on both product terms, and rotate back. The triangle isomorphism criterion [lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso] gives an isomorphism $e:U\to R\lim\mathcal U_\bullet$ with $p^U_n\circ e=c^U_n$ for every $n$. No unique comparison is needed. Define $\gamma=F\circ e:U\to V$. It is an isomorphism. The integral constructible and finite-Tor categories are full and invariant under isomorphism by [lem-weil-integral-ctf-triangulated]; Step 1 consequently places $V$ as well as $U$ in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] to $\mathcal V_\bullet$. Its canonical isomorphism $b^V_n:V\otimes^L_{R_X}B_{n,X}\to V_n$ is the counit comparison, adjoint to the tower projection $p^V_n$. Projection naturality from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] and Step 4 give $p^V_n\circ\gamma=\operatorname{Res}_n(g_n)\circ c^U_n$. For the completed coefficient projection $\pi_n:R_X\to B_{n,X}$, ordinary extension of scalars is left adjoint to restriction: a module map $h:N\to\operatorname{Res}_n P$ corresponds to $x\otimes b\mapsto b h(x)$, with inverse $x\mapsto h(x\otimes1)$. Restriction is exact by [lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact], hence is its own everywhere-defined right derived functor. The left derived extension is everywhere defined by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Therefore [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] gives $-\otimes^L_{R_X}B_{n,X}\dashv\operatorname{Res}_n$. Under this completed-coefficient derived adjunction, the left side is adjoint to $b^V_n\circ(\gamma\otimes^L_{R_X}B_{n,X})$, and the right side is adjoint to $g_n\circ b^U_n$, where $b^U_n:U\otimes^L_{R_X}B_{n,X}\simeq U_n$ is the canonical reduction identification of Step 1. Equality of adjoints proves $b^V_n\circ(\gamma\otimes^L B_{n,X})=g_n\circ b^U_n$ in $D(B_{n,X})$. This is exactly the required reduction identity, with its quotient-coefficient action retained. Effectivity also supplies compatibility of the $b^V_n$ with all normalization maps. The proof neither detects equality of derived morphisms from their stalks nor deduces uniqueness from conservativity.

statement_correction.old_statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of relative dimension $d$, and let

$$
Lf^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!K
$$

in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$, whose reduction at every level $n$ is

statement_correction.what: The imported statement and unit do not assume that X and Y are separated finite-type k-schemes. However Rf^! is only defined on the finite-type geometric domain of def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, and the named finite purity comparisons require separated finite-type k-schemes. Let Y=Spec k and X be a countable disjoint union of Spec k. Its structural map is smooth separated, purely zero-dimensional and not quasi-compact, hence not finite type. Thus the imported hypotheses admit a case where their named Rf^! and gamma are outside their definitions. This is a typing failure, not a claimed counterexample to a separately extended general smooth-purity theorem. The corrected statement explicitly uses separated finite-type X,Y; all conclusions, signs and finite reductions are retained.

unit_error.source_step:
*Step 2 (the adic stage).* Let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ be the normalized system $(K_n)_n$. By
Step 1 the isomorphisms $\gamma_{f,K_n}$ commute with the transition maps
of the system, so they form a morphism of normalized systems, the common
bounds and stratifications being those of $K$ with the same $d$-shift.
The uniform-tower reconstruction realizes that morphism as a single map
$Lf^{*}K(d)[2d]\to Rf^{!}K$ over $\mathcal O_E$ whose reduction at every
level $n$ is $\gamma_{f,K_n}$; a map of towers that is an isomorphism at
every level is an isomorphism, so $\gamma_{f,K}$ is one.
unit_error.failed_inference: The sentence "the common bounds and stratifications being those of K with the same d-shift" is used to invoke lem-weil-pbc-reconstruction-uniform-tower. The current integral definition gives a complete object with constructible reductions and one cohomological interval; finite Tor gives one Tor interval. Neither gives the single finite stratification, covering local complexes L independent of n, and compatible quotient-linear e_n required by def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower. A bound and levelwise constructibility do not supply those data by definition. The reconstruction theorem also restricts functoriality to equipped coherent tower maps: it does not give an arbitrary family a canonical lift. Applying that theorem without establishing these hypotheses is the failing inference in Step 2. The return independently identifies this as a real gap. No claim that common local models can never be proved is made.
unit_error.replacement: Keep finite-level purity and its reduction square. Construct the two coherent normalized DVR towers, lift the compatible gamma_n using lem-weil-pbc-sequential-tower-evaluation-full, and apply the strict total derived-limit functor. A morphism of Roos triangles with levelwise isomorphisms is invertible. Use normalized DVR effectivity, which does not assume local models, for the canonical quotient-linear reduction comparisons; transpose the projection identity under derived extension/restriction to get the specified finite reductions. Source finiteness is proved separately, and target finiteness follows from isomorphism. This is the explicit replacement of the unit Step 2 reconstruction argument, not a claimed application of uniform-tower reconstruction.

$f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of relative dimension $d$, and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ with finite reductions
$K_n\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$. The comparisons
$\gamma_{f,K_n}$ of [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] form a
morphism of normalized systems in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and they induce an isomorphism

$$
Lf^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!K
$$

in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$, whose reduction at every level $n$ is
exactly $\gamma_{f,K_n}$.

proof.text:
By [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity], the reduction of
$\gamma_{f,K_{n+1}}$ along $A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n}$ is
$\gamma_{f,K_n}$, i.e. the comparisons are compatible with the
transition maps of the normalized system; the common bounds and
stratifications of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower] are those
of $K$ with the same $d$-shift. Hence
$(\gamma_{f,K_n})_{n}$ is a morphism of normalized systems, whose
realization under the uniform-tower reconstruction of
[lem-weil-pbc-reconstruction-uniform-tower] is the displayed
isomorphism over $\mathcal O_E$, and the levelwise nature of the
reconstruction gives the compatibility with the reductions.
